description: Ranks customers by total revenue within a date range. Use for any 'biggest / best / top customers' style question.

params.name: from
params.description: Start of the date range, YYYY-MM-DD. Inclusive.

params.name: to
params.description: End of the date range, YYYY-MM-DD. The whole day is included.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many customers to return, capped server-side at 100

example_questions: who are our biggest customers this year
which accounts bring in the most money
rank customers by revenue for Q2
show me our best customers last month
sab se baray customers kaun hain
hamara sab se bara client kaun hai revenue ke hisaab se

follow_up_questions.label: By region
follow_up_questions.prompt: Break that revenue down by sales region

follow_up_questions.label: By category
follow_up_questions.prompt: Break that revenue down by product category

follow_up_questions.label: Top products
follow_up_questions.prompt: Which products sold the most over the same period?

graphql: query TopCustomers($from: LocalDate!, $to: LocalDate!, $limit: Int) { topCustomers(from: $from, to: $to, limit: $limit) { customerId customerName territory revenue orderCount } }
returns: A plain list of customers with their summed revenue, sales region and order count for the period, highest revenue first.
do_not_use_when: The user names one specific customer — use customer(id:) instead. The user asks about revenue over time rather than a ranking — use revenueByPeriod. The user wants headline totals rather than a ranking — use salesSummary.
notes: Dates are the LocalDate scalar, not Date. If the user says 'this year' resolve to Jan 1 of the current year through today. 'Last quarter' means the previous complete calendar quarter. Order data in this database runs 2022-05-30 to 2025-06-29; ranges outside that return an empty list rather than an error.
